inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average count for H1 2026 (1,326.1m, H1 2026 half-year report EPS note). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows via sbc_pct_path, so compounding the count as well would charge dilution twice. Company repurchases ~EUR340m/yr (FY2025 net EUR340.3m) to offset grant dilution, so the flat count is funded, not a convention. The FY2025 EUR111.3m 'capital increase' is the employee share-purchase plan and is part of the same compensation mechanism.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 URD Note 24 'Non-cash share-based compensation expense' EUR174.8m (FY2024 EUR190.4m); same figure in the cash-flow add-back. EquityAwardTaxes is 0 in every year of the Metrics CSV: French-style free-share plans are settled in shares with no net-share-settlement withholding line in financing, so the combined figure equals the add-back. FY2026 guidance: ~EUR115m excluding grants after 30 June 2026.
inputs.fx_note: Statements, flows and the Euronext Paris quote are all EUR; fx_rate 1.0, no conversion. The company's FY2026 guidance FX assumptions (USD 1.17/EUR, JPY 177.1/EUR) affect reported growth only (H1 2026 revenue -1% reported vs +4% constant currency) and are reflected in the year-1 growth driver, not in any price conversion.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:35:08Z (Euronext Paris regular close, Friday; latest completed session as at the Monday valuation date)
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR flows discounted at a EUR-built rate. 10y Bund ~2.7% + mature-market ERP 5.0% x beta ~1.1 (observed post-February-2026 selloff) = cost of equity ~8.2%; EUR1.0bn 5-year bond at 3.375% (Jun 2026) gives after-tax cost of debt ~2.6% at ~10% of capital; textbook WACC 7.3-7.7%. House rate 8.0% in all three scenarios, i.e. ~0.3-0.5pp of conservatism versus the textbook build and roughly 2.5pp below the USD tech default, matching the EUR/USD rate differential and DSY's lower beta. No ad-hoc AI-disruption or governance premium: those risks are charged once, in the bear scenario and its 25% weight. Sensitivity grid runs 6-10%.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. Total cash outflow for leases EUR119.0m in FY2025 (URD supplemental disclosure: EUR89.7m principal in financing + ~EUR10.7m lease interest + short-term/low-value leases), EUR111.6m in FY2024, i.e. 1.9% of revenue; charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path = 1.9%. Lease liabilities (EUR574m at FY2025: 81.0 current + 493.0 non-current) are therefore EXCLUDED from total_debt; H1 2026 total_debt 3,377.7 = borrowings only (1,237.5 current + 2,140.2 non-current, H1 2026 Note 12). da_pct_path (2.1%) is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation so the lease is not charged twice: FY2025 D&A 552.7 = 337.6 acquired-intangible amortisation (non-IFRS reconciliation) + ~85 ROU depreciation (approximates the 89.7 principal) + ~130 PP&E and software (Note 24: PP&E depreciation 208.2 less ROU; intangibles 344.5 less 337.6 acquired). Note last_fcf follows the house formula (reported - SBC - interest income) and does NOT yet deduct the lease cash; on the fully lease-adjusted basis the projections use, FY2025 owner FCF was EUR1,025.5m (16.4% of revenue).
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests EUR5.4m at FY2025 after the EUR253.8m buy-out of the Centric Software minority in 2025 (Note 24). Immaterial: consolidated flows are used with no NCI deduction in the bridge; the omission is worth <EUR0.01/share. NetIncomeInclNCI 1,187.6 vs attributable 1,196.0 in FY2025 is a loss-making minority, not leakage.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: operating company, software/PLM) with the non-US adaptations: EUR-built WACC, lease treatment (B), interest income stripped against a net cash pile of EUR2,282m (>2x owner FCF), NCI immaterial. First valuation of this ticker; no MEMORY.md entry. BASIS OF THE EBITDA LINE: ebitda_margin_path is IFRS EBITDA + SBC, i.e. pre-SBC, pre-IFRS-16-lease, but AFTER restructuring, acquisition costs and social charges on share plans (FY2025: 1,907.0 + 174.8 = 2,081.8, 33.4%; FY2024 34.2%; FY2023 33.6%; FY2022 36.7%; FY2021 36.4%; H1 2026 33.8% vs H1 2025 29.9%). It is deliberately NOT the company's non-IFRS operating margin (32.0% FY2025, guided 32.2-32.6% FY2026), which excludes those recurring charges. CASH TAX: 24% flat in all scenarios. FY2025 cash tax paid (EUR255.3m, 15.4% of pre-amortisation EBIT) understates the run-rate: income tax expense 270.8 includes a deferred-tax BENEFIT of 131.6 (146.0 in FY2024) from the DTL unwind on non-deductible Medidata intangibles amortisation, so current tax was ~402 (24.3% of the component EBIT of ~1,658; FY2024 25.2%), and the tax payable grew 75.2 in 2025 and 42.9 in 2024. Taxing pre-amortisation EBIT at 24% is the economically right treatment: the amortisation is sunk purchase price and gives no cash shield. WORKING CAPITAL: wc_capture_pct = -75% of the YoY revenue change in all scenarios. Trade receivables and contract assets grew EUR196.7m (FY2025) and EUR347.7m (FY2024) against revenue growth of EUR22m and EUR262m, because multi-year subscription term licences are recognised upfront under IFRS 15 but invoiced annually; ex the tax-payable timing the operating-asset drag was ~EUR180-200m/yr. -75% of a ~EUR280m revenue increase charges ~EUR210m/yr in the growth years, fading to ~EUR120m as growth decelerates and the subscription mix matures. ARISGLOBAL: the ~USD1.8bn (up to USD2.0bn with earn-outs, ~EUR1.5-1.7bn) acquisition announced 23 July 2026 is pending and will consume roughly two-thirds of the 30 June 2026 net cash on closing in H2 2026. It is EXCLUDED from both the flows and the bridge, i.e. treated as value-neutral at the purchase price; at an implied 10x+ revenue, any shortfall against an 8% return on the EUR1.5bn is a direct deduction from these values (each 1pp of under-return on cost ~ EUR0.01/share/yr, capitalised ~EUR0.2/share). Enalean (March 2026) and Contentserv (2025, EUR203.5m) are already in the H1 2026 balance sheet. YEAR-1 SANITY: base FY2026 owner FCF ~EUR1,230m (19.4% of revenue) versus FY2025 lease-adjusted actual EUR1,025.5m (16.4%); the uplift is SBC guided down ~EUR55m, the receivables build assumed to halve from the FY2024-25 pace, partly offset by the 24% cash tax (~EUR145m above cash actually paid in FY2025). Price is the Friday 23 Oct 2026 regular close, not an after-hours print.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: FY2026 guidance (revenue EUR6,296-6,416m, +1-3% reported / +3-5% constant currency) for year 1, stepping to ~4.5% constant-currency growth in FY2027-29 as the software cc run-rate (+4-5% in 2025-26, 3DEXPERIENCE +10%, cloud +11%) persists and automotive/Medidata stop shrinking; decelerating to 2.5% terminal. Equity CAGR (6.3% / 11.5%) is rejected as the anchor because it compounds retained earnings on a net-cash balance sheet and overstates business growth; revenue 3yr CAGR 3.2% is the closest observed analogue.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 11.5% diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR 7.0% and from revenue 3yr CAGR 3.2%: shareholders' equity grew by retained net income on a net-cash balance sheet (payout + buybacks ~55% of net income), not by faster business growth. EPS 5yr CAGR 19.3% is inflated by the depressed FY2020 base (COVID, peak Medidata amortisation); the 3yr EPS CAGR of 8.7% is the representative figure.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income - lease principal repayment): FY2020 828.4, FY2021 1,228.8, FY2022 1,084.4, FY2023 1,007.9, FY2024 1,017.4, FY2025 1,054.8 (EUR m). Lease principal only is deducted in the history because the total lease outflow is disclosed only for FY2024-25 (111.6 / 119.0 vs principal 79.7 / 89.7). Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (-0.9%) is well below reported FCF 3yr CAGR (+1.8%) and far below revenue (+3.2%): interest income rose from EUR39.8m to EUR150.0m over FY2022-25 and SBC stayed ~3% of revenue, so an increasing share of reported FCF growth was earned on the cash pile and paid for in stock, not generated by operations. Owner FCF has been flat at ~EUR1.0-1.1bn for four years.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 at 1.5% sits in the lower half of the maintained FY2026 guidance (+1-3% reported) because H1 2026 was -1% reported and H2 must deliver ~+4.8% reported with roughly neutral FX, after two consecutive cuts (Oct 2025, Feb 2026). FY2027-29 at 4.5% is the constant-currency software run-rate; it assumes automotive and Medidata flatten rather than recover and gives no credit to the 2029 EPS-doubling ambition (which needs ~8-10% revenue growth) or to ArisGlobal (value-neutral).
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC pre-lease IFRS EBITDA margin from 33.8% (FY2025 33.4% + the ~0.4pp improvement embedded in the 32.2-32.6% non-IFRS guidance) to 35.5% by year 8: operating leverage on a 83%-recurring base plus cloud scale, still below the 36.4-36.7% of FY2021-22. SBC recovers from the price-depressed 1.9% guided for 2026 to a 2.5% long-run level, below the ~3% 2019-2025 average because the company is mature.
base.narrative: Core PLM franchise (CATIA/ENOVIA/SIMULIA, SOLIDWORKS) grows mid-single-digit in constant currency on 25-year customer relationships; 3DEXPERIENCE and cloud keep growing ~10%; Medidata stabilises at a lower level rather than recovers; AI (3D UNIV+RSES, NVIDIA/Mistral partnerships) is monetised modestly and is not disruptive to the installed base in the forecast window. Margins expand slowly; the subscription transition keeps absorbing ~EUR150-200m/yr of cash in contract assets before fading.

bull.narrative: FY2026 lands at the top of guidance, then automotive capex and clinical-trial starts recover together in 2027-28 while AI-native offerings (Virtual Companions, Generative Experiences, Virtual Twins as a Service) add a paid layer on top of the installed base, lifting cc growth to 6.5-7%. Margin returns to the FY2021-22 pre-SBC level of ~37.5% on cloud scale and mix. Even this case delivers roughly 60-70% of the 'double EPS by 2029' ambition on an owner-FCF basis; the November 2026 Capital Markets Day is a re-rating catalyst rather than a reset. Slightly higher capex (2.7%) funds cloud/AI infrastructure.

bear.narrative: A third guidance miss: FY2026 revenue flat as Q4 licence deals slip, then AI-native CAD/simulation entrants (Anthropic-backed tools, Prometheus) and Siemens/PTC bundling cap pricing on renewals so cc growth settles at 1.5%; Medidata keeps shrinking with clinical-trial starts; automotive stays weak. Retention pressure after the share-price crash pushes SBC back to 2.8% of revenue and margin compresses ~2.5pp to 31% as R&D is protected. The 2029 EPS target is withdrawn at the November 2026 CMD and ArisGlobal integration disappoints. Terminal multiple capped at 15x FCF and terminal growth 1.5% for a franchise perceived as ex-growth; WACC is held at 8.0% so the risk is charged in the flows and the weight, not a second time in the rate.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-single-digit constant-currency growth from a 83%-recurring PLM franchise with 25-year customer relationships; 3DEXPERIENCE/cloud ~+10%, Medidata stabilises, AI additive but modest; margin drifts up ~1.7pp over eight years; subscription transition keeps absorbing cash in contract assets until growth slows. No credit to the 2029 EPS-doubling ambition or to ArisGlobal.
scenario_narratives.bull: Automotive and clinical-trial cycles recover together in 2027-28 and AI-native offerings become a paid layer on the installed base; cc growth 6.5-7%, pre-SBC margin back to the FY2021-22 ~37.5%; November 2026 CMD re-rates the stock rather than resetting targets.
scenario_narratives.bear: Third guidance miss, AI-native entrants and peer bundling cap renewal pricing, Medidata and automotive keep shrinking; growth settles at 1.5%, margin compresses to 31%, SBC rises to 2.8% on retention pressure; 15x terminal cap for an ex-growth franchise.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear weight raised to 25% because visibility has demonstrably deteriorated (two guidance cuts in four months, the co-founder Chairman's abrupt February 2026 exit, an unresolved AI-disruption narrative that will be tested at the 17 November 2026 CMD) and because the bear case is a slow-growth franchise, not insolvency, so it does not warrant going higher. Bull weight cut to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right at once: an automotive capex recovery, a clinical-trial-start recovery for Medidata, and paid AI monetisation on the installed base. Base keeps the 50% default: the recurring-revenue core at +4-5% cc is what the company has actually delivered through the downturn.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF with SBC fully expensed, interest income stripped against the EUR2.28bn net cash it is earned on, leases charged as operating cost, acquired-intangible amortisation treated as sunk (no cash D&A, no tax shield: cash tax at the 24% current-tax run-rate rather than the 15% flattered by the DTL unwind), and the subscription-transition receivables build modelled as negative working-capital capture on revenue growth. Dassault is a high-quality, slow-compounding franchise whose reported FCF has been flat at ~EUR1.0-1.1bn on an owner basis for four years while interest income and SBC did the growing; the valuation therefore rests on whether mid-single-digit cc growth and modest margin expansion resume, not on the 2029 EPS-doubling ambition, which is given no credit in the base case. ArisGlobal is treated as value-neutral at its purchase price. The house/street band is narrow (SBC ~2.5% of revenue) so the SBC treatment is not what decides this one; the cash tax rate and the working-capital drag are.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cash tax: the model charges 24% on pre-amortisation EBIT (current-tax run-rate); if the 17-18% IFRS effective rate proves cash-sustainable (R&D credits, US FDII), base value is understated by roughly EUR2/share. Conversely Pillar 2 and the run-off of amortisation shields could push the rate above 24%.

Working capital: -75% capture of revenue growth charges EUR150-210m/yr of contract-asset build; if the FY2024-25 receivables build was a one-off DSO extension rather than structural, base value is ~EUR1.5-2/share too low; if it persists at EUR300m+/yr it is too high.

ArisGlobal (~EUR1.5-1.7bn, closing H2 2026) is value-neutral in the model; at 10x+ revenue a return on cost below the 8% WACC is a direct deduction, and it uses up two-thirds of the net cash in the bridge.

AI-native disruption of CAD/PLM (Anthropic-backed tools, Prometheus) is carried only through the 25% bear weight and its 1.5% growth / 31% margin path; a faster or broader displacement of licensed engineering software is outside even the bear case.
Terminal value is ~55-60% of base EV at 8% WACC / 2.5% g (Gordon binds just inside the 20x cap); each 1pp of WACC is worth roughly EUR4-5/share.
Governance: GIMD/Dassault family controls ~54% of votes; capital allocation (serial M&A, Centric buy-out, ArisGlobal) is decided without minority consent.
FX: ~39% of software revenue is USD and a material JPY share; a 5% EUR appreciation takes ~2pp off reported growth and the year-1 driver.
Price is the 23 Oct 2026 regular close; the 17 Nov 2026 Capital Markets Day (AI monetisation, 2029 ambition update) is a scheduled event likely to move both the price and the base drivers.
